thread:
Ben (sales): Quick one — AcmeCorp POC asked whether our ISO/ISMS 'scope' language covers SSO(IdP) configuration and shared service accounts. They want an explicit applicability sentence for the vendor questionnaire and for the PoC checklist. Any short, copy-paste wording I can give them?

Chris (security): Short answer: yes for managed SSO in Hosted/Dedicated. For Private deployments we generally say 'customer-managed identity services' and list them out. For shared service accounts we should avoid blanket exclusions — better to call out transient CI runners and third-party dev tools as out-of-scope.

Sara (legal): +1. For customer-facing docs we should use conservative language. Suggested line: `The ISMS scope covers the Redwood Inference control plane, customer data processing, and associated operational controls for Hosted and Dedicated deployments; Private deployments are limited to the customer-managed network and identity components as described.` Use that in SIG/CAIQ answers.

Kai (eng): For the PoC specifically, call out SSO bootstrap steps we do vs what the customer provides. Example: "Redwood configures SP metadata and provisioning for Hosted; customers provide IdP credentials for Private". Also note: shared service accounts used by infra (eg. `infra-ci@example.com`) are ephemeral and logged — we keep them in scope for audit trails, not excluded.

Ben (sales): Nice. Can we add a tiny snippet for the PoC checklist that security can sign off on? They want to know if SSO will be tested in the PoC or deferred to production.

Chris (security): PoC checklist blurb: ```- Authentication: Validate SSO sign-in for a test org (Hosted/Dedicated). For Private, verify SAML/OIDC metadata exchange and successful assertion validation. - Privileged accounts: Ensure shared service accounts are rotated and auditable; list exceptions with justification. - Logs: Confirm access and admin actions are captured in audit logs retained per contract.```

Sara (legal): Also include a line about applicability: `Controls marked N/A in the SIG/CAIQ are not applicable to Private deployments where the customer controls the network and IdP; otherwise controls apply.` Keep it simple.

Ben (sales): Perfect — I'll paste those into the customer email and the Sig/CAIQ free-text fields. @Chris can you flag any controls we should mark as 'customer responsibility' in the CAIQ (ID management, network segmentation for Private)?

Chris (security): Yep — I'll mark ID-01, ID-04 as "customer responsibility for Private" and add notes for network segmentation. Will update the shared CAIQ copy in the repo.

deploy-bot: Deployment to docs-staging succeeded (build 2026.03.18.42).

Ben (sales): Thanks everyone — sending now. If they ask for the Letter of Applicability phrasing, use Sara's sentence as the core and add the PoC checklist above. :thumbsup:
